title: Stack two lists
prompt: Show one list of names: customer names followed by product names. Keep any duplicates, using UNION ALL. Replace the ___.
hints: Both queries must have one column.

cases.name: Different data
cases.setupSql: DELETE FROM order_items; DELETE FROM orders; DELETE FROM products; DELETE FROM customers; INSERT INTO customers VALUES (7, 'Ravi', 'Oslo', 'ravi@mail.test', '2024-05-05'), (8, 'Sara', 'Lima', NULL, '2024-06-06'), (9, 'Tom', 'Oslo', NULL, '2024-07-07'); INSERT INTO products VALUES (7, 'Stool', 'Home', 40.0, 25.0), (8, 'Cup', 'Kitchen', 9.0, 2.0), (9, 'Ink', 'Stationery', 12.5, 6.0); INSERT INTO orders VALUES (11, 7, '2024-02-28', 'shipped'), (12, 8, '2024-03-01', 'pending'), (13, 7, '2024-03-31', 'cancelled'); INSERT INTO order_items VALUES (11, 7, 1, 4.0), (11, 8, 3, NULL), (12, 9, 2, NULL), (13, 8, 1, NULL);

solutions: SELECT name FROM customers UNION ALL SELECT name FROM products;

wrongSolutions.sql: SELECT name FROM customers UNION ALL SELECT category FROM products;

title: Remove duplicates
prompt: Show every different city and category in a single column named value, removing duplicates, using UNION.

cases.name: Different data
cases.setupSql: DELETE FROM order_items; DELETE FROM orders; DELETE FROM products; DELETE FROM customers; INSERT INTO customers VALUES (7, 'Ravi', 'Oslo', 'ravi@mail.test', '2024-05-05'), (8, 'Sara', 'Lima', NULL, '2024-06-06'), (9, 'Tom', 'Oslo', NULL, '2024-07-07'); INSERT INTO products VALUES (7, 'Stool', 'Home', 40.0, 25.0), (8, 'Cup', 'Kitchen', 9.0, 2.0), (9, 'Ink', 'Stationery', 12.5, 6.0); INSERT INTO orders VALUES (11, 7, '2024-02-28', 'shipped'), (12, 8, '2024-03-01', 'pending'), (13, 7, '2024-03-31', 'cancelled'); INSERT INTO order_items VALUES (11, 7, 1, 4.0), (11, 8, 3, NULL), (12, 9, 2, NULL), (13, 8, 1, NULL);

solutions: SELECT city AS value FROM customers UNION SELECT category FROM products;

wrongSolutions.sql: SELECT city AS value FROM customers UNION ALL SELECT category FROM products;
SELECT city AS value FROM customers;

title: Label the rows
prompt: Show each name with a column kind: Customer for customers and Product for products. Sort by kind, then name.
hints: Add a fixed text column to each branch.

cases.name: Different data
cases.setupSql: DELETE FROM order_items; DELETE FROM orders; DELETE FROM products; DELETE FROM customers; INSERT INTO customers VALUES (7, 'Ravi', 'Oslo', 'ravi@mail.test', '2024-05-05'), (8, 'Sara', 'Lima', NULL, '2024-06-06'), (9, 'Tom', 'Oslo', NULL, '2024-07-07'); INSERT INTO products VALUES (7, 'Stool', 'Home', 40.0, 25.0), (8, 'Cup', 'Kitchen', 9.0, 2.0), (9, 'Ink', 'Stationery', 12.5, 6.0); INSERT INTO orders VALUES (11, 7, '2024-02-28', 'shipped'), (12, 8, '2024-03-01', 'pending'), (13, 7, '2024-03-31', 'cancelled'); INSERT INTO order_items VALUES (11, 7, 1, 4.0), (11, 8, 3, NULL), (12, 9, 2, NULL), (13, 8, 1, NULL);

solutions: SELECT name, 'Customer' AS kind FROM customers UNION ALL SELECT name, 'Product' FROM products ORDER BY kind, name;

wrongSolutions.sql: SELECT name, 'Customer' AS kind FROM customers UNION ALL SELECT name, 'Customer' FROM products ORDER BY kind, name;
SELECT name, 'Customer' AS kind FROM customers UNION ALL SELECT name, 'Product' FROM products ORDER BY name;

title: Both sides count
prompt: Show one column, user_id, listing every id found in either users.id or users.referrer_id. Remove NULLs and duplicates.
hints: UNION removes duplicates, and filter NULLs.
solutions: SELECT id AS user_id FROM users UNION SELECT referrer_id FROM users WHERE referrer_id IS NOT NULL;

wrongSolutions.sql: SELECT id AS user_id FROM users UNION ALL SELECT referrer_id FROM users WHERE referrer_id IS NOT NULL;
SELECT id AS user_id FROM users UNION SELECT referrer_id FROM users;

title: Fixed categories
prompt: Using UNION ALL, show exactly three rows in a column named band: Low, Mid, and High. Beside each, show as staff how many employees earn under 50000, from 50000 to 90000, and over 90000.
hints: Each branch counts its own band.

cases.name: Different data
cases.setupSql: DELETE FROM employees; DELETE FROM departments; INSERT INTO departments VALUES (5, 'Design'), (6, 'Finance'), (7, 'Ops'); INSERT INTO employees VALUES (11, 'Ivy', 5, NULL, 90000, '2019-02-01', 900, 'ivy@acme.test'), (12, 'Jon', 5, 11, 70000, '2020-06-15', NULL, NULL), (13, 'Kim', 6, 11, 70000, '2023-03-03', 300, 'kim@acme.test'), (14, 'Leo', NULL, 77, 30000, '2024-08-20', NULL, 'leo@acme.test'), (15, 'Mia', 6, 13, 55000, '2022-12-31', 0, 'mia@acme.test'); UPDATE employees SET salary = 80000 WHERE id = 11; UPDATE employees SET salary = 90000 WHERE id = 12;

solutions: SELECT 'Low' AS band, COUNT(*) AS staff FROM employees WHERE salary < 50000 UNION ALL SELECT 'Mid', COUNT(*) FROM employees WHERE salary BETWEEN 50000 AND 90000 UNION ALL SELECT 'High', COUNT(*) FROM employees WHERE salary > 90000;

wrongSolutions.sql: SELECT CASE WHEN salary < 50000 THEN 'Low' WHEN salary <= 90000 THEN 'Mid' ELSE 'High' END AS band, COUNT(*) AS staff FROM employees GROUP BY band;

SELECT 'Low' AS band, COUNT(*) AS staff FROM employees WHERE salary < 50000 UNION ALL SELECT 'Mid', COUNT(*) FROM employees WHERE salary > 50000 AND salary < 90000 UNION ALL SELECT 'High', COUNT(*) FROM employees WHERE salary > 90000;

title: Fix the branches
prompt: This should list customer names and then product names, with a label, but the branches have different column counts. Fix it so both have name and kind.
hints: Each branch needs the same number of columns.

cases.name: Different data
cases.setupSql: DELETE FROM order_items; DELETE FROM orders; DELETE FROM products; DELETE FROM customers; INSERT INTO customers VALUES (7, 'Ravi', 'Oslo', 'ravi@mail.test', '2024-05-05'), (8, 'Sara', 'Lima', NULL, '2024-06-06'), (9, 'Tom', 'Oslo', NULL, '2024-07-07'); INSERT INTO products VALUES (7, 'Stool', 'Home', 40.0, 25.0), (8, 'Cup', 'Kitchen', 9.0, 2.0), (9, 'Ink', 'Stationery', 12.5, 6.0); INSERT INTO orders VALUES (11, 7, '2024-02-28', 'shipped'), (12, 8, '2024-03-01', 'pending'), (13, 7, '2024-03-31', 'cancelled'); INSERT INTO order_items VALUES (11, 7, 1, 4.0), (11, 8, 3, NULL), (12, 9, 2, NULL), (13, 8, 1, NULL);

solutions: SELECT name, 'C' AS kind FROM customers UNION ALL SELECT name, 'P' FROM products;

wrongSolutions.sql: SELECT name FROM customers UNION ALL SELECT name FROM products;
SELECT name, 'C' AS kind FROM customers;

title: Sorted branches
prompt: Show the single longest session's minutes and the single shortest session's minutes, as two rows, longest first, in a column named minutes.
hints: Wrap each sorted branch in a FROM subquery, as SQLite has no brackets around branches.
solutions: SELECT minutes FROM (SELECT minutes FROM sessions ORDER BY minutes DESC LIMIT 1) UNION ALL SELECT minutes FROM (SELECT minutes FROM sessions ORDER BY minutes LIMIT 1);

wrongSolutions.sql: SELECT MAX(minutes) AS minutes FROM sessions;
SELECT minutes FROM (SELECT minutes FROM sessions ORDER BY minutes LIMIT 1) UNION ALL SELECT minutes FROM (SELECT minutes FROM sessions ORDER BY minutes DESC LIMIT 1);

title: Combined totals
prompt: Show each student_id and the number of graded enrolments plus the number of ungraded enrolments, as a stacked list with kind (Graded or Pending) and total. Skip zeros.

cases.name: Different data
cases.setupSql: DELETE FROM enrolments; DELETE FROM courses; DELETE FROM students; INSERT INTO students VALUES (6, 'Femi', 9), (7, 'Gia', 9), (8, 'Hao', 10); INSERT INTO courses VALUES (5, 'Chemistry', 'Science'), (6, 'Drama', 'Arts'); INSERT INTO enrolments VALUES (11, 6, 5, 60, '2023-autumn'), (12, 6, 5, 60, '2024-spring'), (13, 7, 5, NULL, '2024-spring'), (14, 7, 6, 95, '2024-spring');

solutions: SELECT student_id, 'Graded' AS kind, COUNT(*) AS total FROM enrolments WHERE grade IS NOT NULL GROUP BY student_id UNION ALL SELECT student_id, 'Pending', COUNT(*) FROM enrolments WHERE grade IS NULL GROUP BY student_id;

wrongSolutions.sql: SELECT student_id, 'Graded' AS kind, COUNT(*) AS total FROM enrolments GROUP BY student_id;
SELECT student_id, 'Graded' AS kind, COUNT(*) AS total FROM enrolments WHERE grade IS NOT NULL GROUP BY student_id;
